configuration: Both upstream cases of unittest/joint-universal.cpp: vsRXRY, cross-validating JointModelUniversal against a JointModelComposite of JointModelRX and JointModelRY at an identity body inertia, and vsRandomAxis, the same shape against a JointModelComposite of two JointModelRevoluteUnaligned at oblique axes and a non-trivial body inertia. Both cases run at the all-ones configuration, velocity and acceleration, which upstream writes as literals and which are frozen at exactly those values; vsRandomAxis's body inertia, drawn upstream from Inertia::Random, is frozen too. All of these are read from ic/<ic>/operands.json.
observable: the universal joint cross-validated against the matching two-joint composite through forward kinematics both before and after a velocity is given, the composite subtree inertia, the centre of mass, the nonlinear effects, the joint force, inverse dynamics, forward dynamics, the joint-space inertia and the joint Jacobian, for both an axis-aligned and an oblique-axis pair of joints
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that vsRandomAxis's body inertia and both cases' all-ones configuration, velocity and acceleration are read from ic/ at exactly upstream's values
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero component of every frozen item in ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every component rather than one was measured, not assumed, on this leaf's first check: with a single component per item, 18 of cpp-explog's 48 observables and 6 of cpp-spatial's 76 came back with a spread of exactly zero, because a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one entry of a rotation matrix rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all nine. Every component still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this stays the generic two-ulp noise calibration rather than a physics experiment. A component that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 6.217e-15 absolute, at universal_vsrxry_rnea_reference. 10 of the 52 observables show a spread of exactly zero. 8 are the composite subtree inertia (Ycrb.back()) recorded at the two forwardKinematics-only stages of each case, before crba or computeAllTerms has run: Data's Ycrb array is zero-initialised and untouched by forwardKinematics alone, so both models record an all-zero 6x6 matrix at that point regardless of the frozen inertia, insensitive by construction. The remaining 2 are vsRandomAxis's own rnea torque on both models: this pair was measured, not assumed, to be exactly insensitive to the two-ulp perturbation of the frozen inertia at this configuration and axis pair, unlike vsRXRY's own rnea, which does move; no structural argument (an axis or a lever lying exactly on the joint axis, as in cpp-joint-revolute's nle case) was found for it, so it is reported as a measured floating-point coincidence rather than a claimed mechanism, and its bound rests on the physical argument in the warrant.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for every graded value of this check (measured on the worker, x86_64, inside the env image, 2026-09-14), so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal, on the worker (x86_64, inside the env image, 2026-09-14); every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantities are the universal joint cross-validated against the matching two-joint composite through forward kinematics, the composite subtree inertia, the centre of mass, the nonlinear effects, the joint force, inverse dynamics, forward dynamics, the joint-space inertia and the joint Jacobian, in SI units and in the coordinate order the joint model fixes, which is part of the input and not something an implementation chooses. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 8.80e+00, it admits about 1.09e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a transposed motion subspace, a wrong axis convention, a rotation composed in the wrong order, or a sign error in the coupling between the two DOFs each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+1 in these units, six to ten decades above the bound, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value of this check lands 8,084,123 times over it. Every upstream identity also stays active, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these expressions differs by about n eps |x|, roughly 30 * 2.2e-16 * 8.80e+00, which is decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 604 graded values by 6.217e-15, using 5.928e-06 of the bound, that is 168,688 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
